newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher on tight liquidity.

text.p: Tightening liquidity in the banking system and easing quarter-end U.S. dollar demand pushed the recently depreciating Taiwan dollar to a higher close on Tuesday. Dealers expected the rate to consolidate.
The local unit closed at T$27.885, back from an intra-day high of T$27.880, against Monday's T$27.892 finish.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$253.5 million.

Dealers said the need for the Taiwan dollar intensified as the recent red hot stock market continued to suck funds out of the banking system, prompting investors to sell U.S. dollars in exchange for Taiwan dollars.
At 0800 GMT, the the overnight interbank rate was at 8.375 percent against Monday's 8.323 close.
The local unit would consolidate around the current level, dealers said.
"With the U.S. dollar demand easing and money rates surging, the depreciation pressure for the Taiwan dollar will likely ease for a while," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
A narrow T$27.86-89 was seen for Wednesday.
